name: Can Tho food
summary: Can Tho eats on the water at dawn, on Đề Thám in town, and at the garden tables of Mỹ Khánh. Start with hủ tiếu handed across from a noodle boat at Cái Răng, the city’s breakfast bowl.
body: Mornings at Cái Răng are a bowl passed across the gunwale while the wholesale boats trade: hủ tiếu, bún riêu, and bún chả cá, with cà phê vợt from the coffee boat. Back in town, lunch is nem nướng Cái Răng over bánh hỏi, and dinner is canh chua, the city’s sour soup. The city’s plates also include bánh xèo, lẩu mắm, grilled snakehead, and fried shrimp cake.

Đề Thám is the food street and a primer in southern cooking; sit wherever it is busiest. Bún nước lèo comes from Soc Trang, 60 km southeast, but you eat it here on Đề Thám and at Mỹ Khánh. Elephant-ear fish and fried pumpkin flowers are Mekong plates rather than Can Tho inventions, and Châu Đốc serves them too.
specialtiesLead: Hủ tiếu, bánh xèo, and canh chua lead. The rest of the city’s plates follow by where you eat them: the boats, the gardens, the quay, and the dinner tables along the Hậu.

sections.heading: Can Tho plates
paragraphs: These plates belong to the city, the quay, Cồn Sơn, and Mỹ Khánh: boat fruit, charcoal pork, garden hot pots, and the riverside dinner sampler. Fried shrimp cake and bánh cống are two different snacks.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: These plates are eaten in Can Tho but belong to the wider delta. Elephant-ear fish and fried pumpkin flowers are Mekong classics, and bún nước lèo comes from Soc Trang; eat it on Đề Thám, at Mỹ Khánh, or in Tra Vinh on the way in.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: Eat everyday Can Tho on the boats, on Đề Thám, at the night market and the old market, at the Mỹ Khánh garden tables, and along the quay snack row.

spots.name: Cai Rang boats
spots.note: Breakfast on the water while the wholesale boats trade: hủ tiếu, bún riêu, cà phê vợt, and bún chả cá. Be on the water early. The listing leaves boat hire as đang cập nhật. Another account gives 300,000–700,000 VND a boat, depending on the number of guests.

spots.name: De Tham
spots.note: Can Tho’s food street and a primer in southern cooking. Sit wherever it is busiest.

spots.name: Ninh Kieu night market
spots.address: Đường Hai Bà Trưng, phường Ninh Kiều
spots.note: Fruit, seafood, clothes, jewelry, and handicrafts along a paved lane. Stalls set up around 16:00 and trade from 17:00 to 22:00.

spots.name: Can Tho old market
spots.address: Hai Bà Trưng, phường Ninh Kiều
spots.note: The old market hall on Hai Bà Trưng sits on the Ninh Kiều quay walk with Chùa Ông. Its first building dates from around 1915.

spots.name: My Khanh garden tables
spots.address: 335 Lộ Vòng Cung, about 10 km from the centre
spots.note: Eat the garden plates at midday after the fruit orchards: cá rô kho tộ, cá lóc nướng trui, lẩu cua đồng, bún nước lèo, and bánh xèo.

spots.name: Quay snack row
spots.address: The road to Bến Ninh Kiều
spots.note: From about 16:00 to 19:00 the quay stalls sell xôi bắp, xôi đậu phộng, xôi trắng, barbecue, bánh xèo, bread, and sweet potato. Eat on the spot or on a bench in the park.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Dawn on the Cái Răng boats is bún riêu, cà phê vợt, and bún chả cá, along with the hủ tiếu above. Be on the water early in the morning.

seoTitle: Can Tho food: boats, De Tham, My Khanh
seoDescription: Hủ tiếu at Cái Răng, bánh xèo, canh chua, Đề Thám, and the Mỹ Khánh garden plates. Soc Trang’s bún nước lèo is served here too.
